question: Who among the following travelers visited India in the 7th century CE?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• **Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**, a Chinese traveler, visited India during the **7th century CE**. He is known for his detailed accounts of Indian society, culture, and religion during the reign of **Harsha (606–647 CE)**. 
• Xuanzang came to India primarily to study Buddhism and collect sacred Buddhist texts. He spent around **17 years** in India, traveling extensively across the subcontinent. 
• During his time in India, Xuanzang visited major Buddhist sites such as **Nalanda University, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, and Kushinagar**. He studied at Nalanda, one of the most prestigious learning centers of the time. 
• Xuanzang documented his journey in the text titled **"Great Tang Records on the Western Regions" (Da Tang Xi Yu Ji)**, which provides invaluable insights into the political, social, and religious conditions of 7th-century India. 
• He described the flourishing of Buddhism in India, the caste system, the structure of Indian cities, and the administration under Emperor Harsha, making his records a significant historical source for understand
